To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IoT Architectural Framework is an open and extensible reference model for the design of IoT solutions.
the IoT ARM provides a reference model for the IoT domain, which can be used to design, develop and implement IoT architectures, solutions and systems.
the ARM is a comprehensive and generic model, which is applicable in any IoT domain and which can be used to design IoT systems and solutions in an efficient way.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects of IoT: - The IoT architectural reference model and how it is structured - The process for generating IoT architectures - The IoT reference architecture and how it can be used to develop IoT solutions - Best practices for using the IoT ARM - The IoT reference platform and its components - The IoT reference implementation and how it can help to validate IoT architectures - The use of the IoT ARM to create IoT solutions in different application areas - The role of the IoT ARM in the IoT standards landscape
the design of IoT solutions and the development of an ARM to support the creation of such IoT solutions.
the creation of an IoT ecosystem and a reference model that will allow the creation of an interoperable IoT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IoT ARM is a reference model for the development of IoT solutions, providing a holistic view on the IoT ecosystem and its components.
this book is the first of its kind to provide an overview and in-depth guidance on the IoT ARM.
the book provides a comprehensive overview of the IoT ARM, which is the result of the IoT A European project.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ARM provides a framework that allows the creation of IoT solutions and the integration of existing systems and platforms.
the ARM is a framework that provides guidance on how to develop IoT systems, architectures and applications.
the ARM provides a common ground and a shared vocabulary for all stakeholders in the IoT domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ARM is a generic framework that can be used for a wide range of IoT applications, including Smart Cities and Smart Buildings, Industry 4.0, Smart Agriculture, Smart Grids and Smart Health.
the ARM is not a rigid framework that must be used in a specific way.
IoT is more than a technology; it is a new paradigm for designing and building solutions.
